title: Chemistry: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank

toc.title: 5.4 Classification of Elements and the Periodic Table
5.5 Chemical Bonding and Shapes of Molecules

html:
Group A of the NEB Grade 11 Chemistry paper is eleven one-mark multiple-choice questions, drawn from across the seventeen units of the CDC syllabus. This chapter drills every unit in order. Each section opens with a high-yield facts table (the formulae, reagents and trends the objective questions keep returning to), then gives six to eight MCQs, then an answer key in which every answer carries a one-line reason and, where a wrong option encodes a real misconception, names it.

What Group A actually tests

Almost nothing in Group A is a long calculation. It tests four things: a definition or name, a formula or reagent, a one-step calculation (a mole, a ratio, an oxidation number), or a misconception offered as a distractor. If an MCQ is taking you more than ninety seconds, you have misread it.

No question here carries a year tag — and that is deliberate

NEB does not publish its Grade 11 question papers, and this book could not verify any item against an official released paper. Rather than print a year it cannot stand behind, it prints none. What it can stand behind is the syllabus weighting (General and Physical 48 h, Inorganic 35 h, Organic 30 h, Applied 15 h of 128), and every question below is built from it. Treat this as a bank of exam-shaped questions, not a leaked paper.

5.1 Foundation and Fundamentals

High-yield fact Value / form
1 amu \tfrac{1}{12} of the mass of one carbon-12 atom (1.66\times10^{-27}\ \text{kg})
Relative molecular mass sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in the formula
Molecular formula n\times empirical formula; n = \dfrac{\text{molar mass}}{\text{empirical formula mass}}
Mass percentage of an element \dfrac{\text{mass of the element in one mole}}{\text{molar mass}}\times100
Radical a group of atoms behaving as one unit and carrying a charge, e.g. \text{NH}_4^{+}, \text{SO}_4^{2-}
  1. One atomic mass unit is equal to [1]athe mass of one hydrogen atomb\tfrac{1}{12} the mass of a carbon-12 atomcthe mass of one proton exactlydthe mass of one electron
  2. The empirical formula of glucose, \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6, is [1]a\text{CH}b\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2c\text{CH}_2\text{O}d\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3
  3. The percentage of oxygen in water (\text{H}=1, \text{O}=16) is [1]a11.1 %b50 %c88.9 %d94.4 %
  4. Which of the following is a radical? [1]a\text{NaCl}b\text{NH}_4^{+}c\text{CO}_2d\text{H}_2\text{O}
  5. The relative molecular mass of \text{CaCO}_3 (\text{Ca}=40, \text{C}=12, \text{O}=16) is [1]a56b84c100d116
  6. A compound has empirical formula \text{CH} and relative molecular mass 78. Its molecular formula is [1]a\text{C}_2\text{H}_2b\text{C}_4\text{H}_4c\text{C}_6\text{H}_6d\text{C}_8\text{H}_8
Answers — 5.1

1. (b) — the definition of the amu.

2. (c) — divide the subscripts 6:12:6 by 6.

3. (c) — 16/18 = 0.889; (a) is the hydrogen percentage, a classic distractor.

4. (b) — \text{NH}_4^{+} is a charged group that moves as a unit.

5. (c) — 40 + 12 + 48 = 100; (b) is \text{MgCO}_3.

6. (c) — 78/13 = 6, so \text{C}_6\text{H}_6.

5.2 Stoichiometry

High-yield fact Value / form
Avogadro constant 6.022\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}
Molar volume at STP (273 K, 1 atm) 22.4\ \text{L mol}^{-1}
Vapour density \text{V.D.} = \dfrac{M}{2}
Laws conservation of mass (Lavoisier); definite proportions (Proust); multiple proportions (Dalton); reciprocal proportions (Richter); Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes
Percentage yield \dfrac{\text{experimental yield}}{\text{theoretical yield}}\times100
Limiting reactant the reactant used up first; it fixes the amount of product
  1. The number of molecules in 0.5 mol of a gas is [1]a6.022\times10^{23}b3.011\times10^{23}c1.2\times10^{24}d6.022\times10^{22}
  2. The volume at STP of 8\ \text{g} of oxygen (\text{O}_2) is [1]a2.8\ \text{L}b5.6\ \text{L}c11.2\ \text{L}d22.4\ \text{L}
  3. The vapour density of a gas of molar mass 44\ \text{g mol}^{-1} is [1]a22b44c88d11
  4. \text{H}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \to 2\text{HCl}. The mass of HCl formed from 2\ \text{g} of hydrogen with excess chlorine is [1]a36.5\ \text{g}b71\ \text{g}c73\ \text{g}d146\ \text{g}
  5. In CO and \text{CO}_2, 12\ \text{g} of carbon combines with 16\ \text{g} and 32\ \text{g} of oxygen. This illustrates the law of [1]aconservation of massbdefinite proportionscmultiple proportionsdreciprocal proportions
  6. If the theoretical yield is 20\ \text{g} and 15\ \text{g} is obtained, the percentage yield is [1]a25 %b75 %c80 %d133 %
  7. Which postulate of Dalton's atomic theory is no longer accepted? [1]aatoms combine in simple whole-number ratiosbatoms of different elements differ in masscatoms are indivisibledcompounds form by combination of atoms
Answers — 5.2

1. (b) — 0.5\times6.022\times10^{23}.

2. (b) — 8/32 = 0.25 mol; 0.25\times22.4 = 5.6\ \text{L}.

3. (a) — M/2 = 22.

4. (c) — 2\ \text{g} is 1 mol of \text{H}_2, giving 2 mol HCl = 73\ \text{g}; (a) forgets the factor of two.

5. (c) — the oxygen masses 16 : 32 = 1 : 2 for a fixed mass of carbon.

6. (b) — 15/20\times100.

7. (c) — atoms are divisible into electrons, protons and neutrons.

5.3 Atomic Structure

High-yield fact Value / form
Quantum numbers n (size, energy), l (shape: 0 to n-1), m_l (orientation: -l to +l), m_s (\pm\tfrac{1}{2})
Electrons in a shell 2n^{2}
Orbitals in s, p, d, f 1, 3, 5, 7
de Broglie wavelength \lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}
Heisenberg \Delta x\cdot\Delta p \ge \dfrac{h}{4\pi}
Exceptions Cr: [\text{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}; Cu: [\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^{1}
Rules Aufbau (lowest energy first); Pauli (no two electrons with the same four quantum numbers); Hund (single occupancy of degenerate orbitals first)
  1. The number of orbitals in a d subshell is [1]a1b3c5d7
  2. The maximum number of electrons in the shell with n = 3 is [1]a8b10c18d32
  3. The electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is [1]a[\text{Ar}]3d^{4}4s^{2}b[\text{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}c[\text{Ar}]3d^{6}d[\text{Ar}]4s^{2}4p^{4}
  4. The quantum number that determines the shape of an orbital is [1]aprincipalbazimuthalcmagneticdspin
  5. Electrons occupy degenerate orbitals singly before pairing, according to [1]aHund's rulebPauli's exclusion principlecAufbau principledHeisenberg's principle
  6. The number of unpaired electrons in \text{Fe}^{3+} (Z = 26) is [1]a1b3c4d5
  7. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle states that [1]aelectrons move in fixed orbitsbposition and momentum cannot both be known exactlycno two electrons have the same four quantum numbersdmatter has no wave nature
Answers — 5.3

1. (c) — l = 2 gives 2l + 1 = 5 orbitals.

2. (c) — 2n^{2} = 18.

3. (b) — a half-filled d subshell is more stable; (a) is the unadjusted Aufbau answer.

4. (b) — l gives s (spherical), p (dumb-bell).

5. (a) — Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity.

6. (d) — \text{Fe}\ 3d^{6}4s^{2} loses the 4s pair and one 3d electron, leaving 3d^{5}: five unpaired.

7. (b) — (a) is Bohr's model and (c) is Pauli's principle.

5.4 Classification of Elements and the Periodic Table

High-yield fact Value / form
Modern periodic law properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers
Effective nuclear charge Z_{eff} = Z - S (S = shielding constant)
Across a period (left to right) atomic radius falls; ionization energy and electronegativity rise; metallic character falls
Down a group atomic radius rises; ionization energy and electronegativity fall
Electronegativity (Pauling) F = 4.0 (highest); O = 3.5; N = 3.0; Cl = 3.0
Electron affinity Cl has the largest magnitude, not F (small size, repulsion)
  1. The most electronegative element is [1]aoxygenbchlorinecfluorinednitrogen
  2. Which has the largest atomic radius? [1]aLibNacKdRb
  3. Across a period from left to right the first ionization energy generally [1]aincreasesbdecreasescstays constantdfirst falls then rises sharply
  4. The halogen with the highest electron affinity (magnitude) is [1]aFbClcBrdI
  5. The correct order of ionic radii of the isoelectronic ions \text{Na}^{+}, \text{Mg}^{2+}, \text{Al}^{3+} is [1]a\text{Na}^{+} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Al}^{3+}b\text{Al}^{3+} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Na}^{+}call equald\text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Na}^{+} > \text{Al}^{3+}
  6. An element of atomic number 17 belongs to [1]as-block, group 1bd-block, group 7cp-block, group 17dp-block, group 7
Answers — 5.4

1. (c) — F has the highest Pauling value, 4.0.

2. (d) — radius grows down the group; Rb is the lowest in the list.

3. (a) — the nuclear charge rises with no extra shell (small dips at Group 13 and 16 are exceptions).

4. (b) — fluorine's small 2p subshell repels the incoming electron, so Cl exceeds F.

5. (a) — same electrons, more protons pull harder: \text{Na}^{+} is the largest.

6. (c) — Cl, [\text{Ne}]3s^{2}3p^{5}, is group 17 of the p-block (IUPAC numbering); (d) uses the old numbering.

5.5 Chemical Bonding and Shapes of Molecules

Species Shape Hybridization Bond angle
\text{BeF}_2, \text{CO}_2 linear sp 180^{\circ}
\text{BF}_3 trigonal planar sp^{2} 120^{\circ}
\text{CH}_4 tetrahedral sp^{3} 109.5^{\circ}
\text{NH}_3 trigonal pyramidal sp^{3} 107^{\circ}
\text{H}_2\text{O} bent (V-shaped) sp^{3} 104.5^{\circ}
\text{PCl}_5 trigonal bipyramidal sp^{3}d 90^{\circ}, 120^{\circ}
\text{SF}_6 octahedral sp^{3}d^{2} 90^{\circ}
  1. The shape of the ammonia molecule is [1]atetrahedralbtrigonal pyramidalcplanardlinear
  2. The hybridization of boron in \text{BF}_3 is [1]aspbsp^{2}csp^{3}dsp^{3}d
  3. The bond angle in water is about [1]a90^{\circ}b104.5^{\circ}c109.5^{\circ}d120^{\circ}
  4. Which molecule has zero dipole moment? [1]a\text{H}_2\text{O}b\text{NH}_3c\text{CO}_2d\text{HCl}
  5. The strongest hydrogen bonding occurs in [1]aHClb\text{H}_2\text{S}cHBrdHF
  6. A coordinate covalent bond is present in [1]a\text{CH}_4b\text{NH}_4^{+}cNaCld\text{H}_2
  7. The shape of \text{SF}_6 is [1]atetrahedralbtrigonal bipyramidalcoctahedraldsquare planar
Answers — 5.5

1. (b) — three bond pairs and one lone pair; (a) ignores the lone pair.

2. (b) — three bond pairs and no lone pair give sp^{2}, trigonal planar.

3. (b) — two lone pairs compress the angle below 109.5^{\circ}.

4. (c) — the two C=O dipoles of the linear molecule cancel.

5. (d) — F is the most electronegative and smallest; HF forms the strongest H-bonds.

6. (b) — the lone pair of N is donated to \text{H}^{+}.

7. (c) — six bond pairs, no lone pair.

5.6 Oxidation and Reduction

High-yield fact Value / form
Oxidation loss of electrons; increase in oxidation number
Reduction gain of electrons; decrease in oxidation number
Rules free element = 0; H usually +1; O usually -2 (-1 in peroxides); sum = charge on the ion
Common values S in \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4: +6; Mn in \text{KMnO}_4: +7; Cr in \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7: +6; Cl in \text{HClO}_4: +7
Faraday's laws m = ZIt; 1\ \text{F} = 96\,500\ \text{C} deposits one equivalent
Electrolysis oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode
  1. The oxidation number of chromium in \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 is [1]a+3b+4c+6d+7
  2. In 2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \to 2\text{MgO} the oxidizing agent is [1]aMgb\text{O}_2cMgOdnone
  3. The average oxidation number of sulphur in \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 is [1]a0b+2c+4d+6
  4. The charge needed to deposit one mole of copper from \text{Cu}^{2+} is [1]a96\,500\ \text{C}b144\,750\ \text{C}c193\,000\ \text{C}d289\,500\ \text{C}
  5. Reduction takes place at the [1]acathodebanodecsalt bridgedelectrolyte
  6. The oxidation number of manganese is highest in [1]a\text{MnO}_2b\text{MnSO}_4c\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4d\text{KMnO}_4
Answers — 5.6

1. (c) — 2x + 2(+1) + 7(-2) = 0 gives x = +6.

2. (b) — \text{O}_2 gains electrons and so oxidizes Mg.

3. (b) — 2(+1) + 2x + 3(-2) = 0 gives x = +2 on average.

4. (c) — \text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \to \text{Cu} needs 2\times96\,500.

5. (a) — reduction is gain of electrons at the cathode (RED CAT).

6. (d) — \text{MnO}_2 +4, \text{MnSO}_4 +2, \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 +6, \text{KMnO}_4 +7.

5.7 States of Matter

High-yield fact Value / form
Boyle's law P_1V_1 = P_2V_2 at constant T
Charles' law \dfrac{V_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{V_2}{T_2} at constant P (T in kelvin)
Ideal gas equation PV = nRT; R = 8.314\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} = 0.0821\ \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}
Dalton's law P_{total} = P_1 + P_2 + \cdots
Graham's law \dfrac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{M_2}{M_1}}
Real gases deviate at high pressure and low temperature
Solids efflorescent loses water of crystallization to air (\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot10\text{H}_2\text{O}); deliquescent absorbs water and dissolves (\text{CaCl}_2, NaOH)
  1. A gas occupies 2\ \text{L} at 1\ \text{atm}. At constant temperature and 4\ \text{atm} it occupies [1]a0.25\ \text{L}b0.5\ \text{L}c1\ \text{L}d8\ \text{L}
  2. The ratio of the rates of diffusion of \text{H}_2 and \text{O}_2 under the same conditions is [1]a1:4b1:16c4:1d16:1
  3. The value of R in \text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} is [1]a8.314b0.0821c1.987d62.4
  4. A gas at 27^{\circ}\text{C} is heated at constant pressure until its volume doubles. The new temperature is [1]a54^{\circ}\text{C}b300\ \text{K}c327^{\circ}\text{C}d600^{\circ}\text{C}
  5. An efflorescent substance is [1]a\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\cdot10\text{H}_2\text{O}banhydrous \text{CaCl}_2cNaCldconc. \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4
  6. A real gas behaves most ideally at [1]ahigh pressure, low temperatureblow pressure, low temperatureclow pressure, high temperaturedhigh pressure, high temperature
  7. The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which [1]avapour pressure is 1\ \text{atm} alwaysbvapour pressure equals the external pressurecthe liquid freezesdthe surface tension is zero
Answers — 5.7

1. (b) — P_1V_1 = P_2V_2 gives V_2 = 2\times1/4 = 0.5\ \text{L}.

2. (c) — \sqrt{32/2} = 4; the lighter gas diffuses faster.

3. (b) — (a) is in joules; (d) is in \text{L mmHg}-type units.

4. (c) — T doubles in kelvin: 300 \to 600\ \text{K} = 327^{\circ}\text{C}; (a) doubles the Celsius value, the common trap.

5. (a) — washing soda loses water on standing.

6. (c) — molecules are far apart and fast, so forces and volume matter least.

7. (b) — (a) is the normal boiling point only.

5.8 Chemical Equilibrium

High-yield fact Value / form
Law of mass action the rate of a reaction is proportional to the product of the active masses (concentrations) of the reactants
For aA + bB \rightleftharpoons cC + dD K_c = \dfrac{[C]^{c}[D]^{d}}{[A]^{a}[B]^{b}}
K_p and K_c K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}; \Delta n = n_{gas,products} - n_{gas,reactants}
Le Chatelier a system at equilibrium opposes any change imposed on it
Catalyst speeds both rates equally; does not change K or the position
  1. For which reaction is K_p = K_c? [1]a\text{H}_2 + \text{I}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}b\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3c\text{PCl}_5 \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2d2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3
  2. For \text{N}_2\text{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2, \Delta n is [1]a-1b0c+1d+2
  3. Increasing the pressure on \text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3 [1]ashifts it to the leftbshifts it to the rightchas no effectdchanges K_c
  4. A catalyst in a reversible reaction [1]ashifts the equilibrium to the rightbraises K_cchelps equilibrium to be reached faster without changing itdstops the reverse reaction
  5. The K_c expression for \text{PCl}_5 \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2 is [1]a\dfrac{[\text{PCl}_5]}{[\text{PCl}_3][\text{Cl}_2]}b\dfrac{[\text{PCl}_3][\text{Cl}_2]}{[\text{PCl}_5]}c[\text{PCl}_3][\text{Cl}_2]d[\text{PCl}_5]
  6. At chemical equilibrium [1]athe forward rate equals the reverse ratebthe reaction stopscconcentrations of reactants and products are equaldthe forward rate is zero
Answers — 5.8

1. (a) — \Delta n = 2 - 2 = 0.

2. (c) — 2 - 1 = +1.

3. (b) — the right side has fewer gas moles (2 against 4).

4. (c) — a catalyst changes the rate, not the position.

5. (b) — products over reactants, each to the power of its coefficient.

6. (a) — equilibrium is dynamic; (c) confuses equal rates with equal concentrations.

5.9 Chemistry of Non-metals

High-yield fact Value / form
Heavy water \text{D}_2\text{O} (deuterium oxide); used as a moderator in reactors
Ozone \text{O}_3; bent; depleted by CFCs; turns moist starch–iodide paper blue
Ring test brown ring of [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{NO}]^{2+} at the junction of acid and \text{FeSO}_4 solution
Kipp's apparatus \text{FeS} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \to \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{S}
Oxidation number of N +5 in \text{HNO}_3; +3 in \text{HNO}_2; -3 in \text{NH}_3
Halogens \text{F}_2 and \text{Cl}_2 gases; \text{Br}_2 liquid; \text{I}_2 solid; oxidizing power \text{F}_2 > \text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2
Fullerene \text{C}_{60}, buckminsterfullerene
Thiosulphate \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3\cdot5\text{H}_2\text{O} ("hypo")
  1. The brown ring in the nitrate ring test is due to [1]a\text{FeSO}_4b[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5\text{NO}]^{2+}c\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3d\text{NO}_2
  2. The gas prepared in a Kipp's apparatus from \text{FeS} is [1]a\text{H}_2b\text{CO}_2c\text{H}_2\text{S}d\text{SO}_2
  3. Depletion of the ozone layer is mainly caused by [1]a\text{CO}_2bchlorofluorocarbonsc\text{CH}_4d\text{N}_2
  4. Heavy water has the formula [1]a\text{D}_2\text{O}b\text{H}_2\text{O}_2c\text{H}_2^{18}\text{O} onlyd\text{HDO} only
  5. The allotrope of carbon containing 60 carbon atoms is [1]adiamondbgraphitecbuckminsterfullerenedcharcoal
  6. The oxidation number of nitrogen in \text{HNO}_3 is [1]a+1b+3c+4d+5
  7. The only halogen that is a liquid at room temperature is [1]achlorinebbromineciodinedfluorine
  8. The formula of sodium thiosulphate is [1]a\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4b\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3c\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3d\text{NaHSO}_4
Answers — 5.9

1. (b) — nitric oxide coordinates to \text{Fe}^{2+}.

2. (c) — \text{FeS} with dilute acid gives hydrogen sulphide; (b) comes from marble.

3. (b) — chlorine radicals from CFCs catalyse \text{O}_3 \to \text{O}_2.

4. (a) — deuterium oxide.

5. (c) — the 60-atom cage.

6. (d) — 1 + x - 6 = 0 gives +5.

7. (b) — bromine; mercury is the only liquid metal.

8. (c) — (a) is sulphate and (b) is sulphite, close distractors.

5.10 Chemistry of Metals

High-yield fact Value / form
Calcination heating the ore in limited or no air (carbonates, hydroxides)
Roasting heating the ore in excess air (sulphides)
Flux and slag gangue + flux \to slag (\text{CaO} + \text{SiO}_2 \to \text{CaSiO}_3)
Thermite \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{Al} \to 2\text{Fe} + \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3
Down's process electrolysis of fused NaCl (with \text{CaCl}_2) for sodium
Plaster of Paris \text{CaSO}_4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}; Epsom salt \text{MgSO}_4\cdot7\text{H}_2\text{O}; quick lime CaO; bleaching powder \text{CaOCl}_2
Refining poling (copper); electro-refining (Cu, Zn)
  1. The formula of plaster of Paris is [1]a\text{CaSO}_4\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O}b\text{CaSO}_4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}c\text{CaSO}_4d\text{CaCO}_3
  2. Calcination is heating an ore [1]ain limited or no airbin excess aircwith carbondin an electric current
  3. In Down's process the electrolyte is [1]aaqueous NaClbmolten NaOHcfused NaCl with \text{CaCl}_2daqueous NaOH
  4. Epsom salt is [1]a\text{CaSO}_4\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O}b\text{MgSO}_4\cdot7\text{H}_2\text{O}c\text{ZnSO}_4\cdot7\text{H}_2\text{O}d\text{FeSO}_4\cdot7\text{H}_2\text{O}
  5. In the thermite process the reducing agent is [1]acarbonbhydrogenccarbon monoxidedaluminium
  6. The substance formed when a flux combines with gangue is [1]amattebslagcalloydamalgam
  7. Poling is used in the refining of [1]aironbcoppercaluminiumdzinc
Answers — 5.10

1. (b) — gypsum (a) loses three-quarters of its water on heating to 120^{\circ}\text{C}.

2. (a) — (b) is roasting.

3. (c) — water would give NaOH and \text{H}_2 instead; \text{CaCl}_2 lowers the melting point.

4. (b) — magnesium sulphate heptahydrate.

5. (d) — Al is a stronger reducing agent than Fe.

6. (b) — slag is the fusible product removed from the furnace.

7. (b) — blister copper is stirred with green wood poles to remove \text{Cu}_2\text{O}.

5.11 Bio-inorganic Chemistry

Metal Role
Mg central ion of chlorophyll
Fe haemoglobin (oxygen carrier), cytochromes
Co vitamin \text{B}_{12}
Zn carbonic anhydrase and many enzymes
Na, K nerve impulse; sodium–potassium pump moves 3\ \text{Na}^{+} out and 2\ \text{K}^{+} in
Ca bones, teeth, muscle contraction, blood clotting
Toxic metals Hg (Minamata disease), Pb, As, Cd
  1. The metal at the centre of chlorophyll is [1]aironbmagnesiumccalciumdzinc
  2. The metal in haemoglobin is [1]aironbcopperccobaltdmagnesium
  3. The \text{Na}^{+}/\text{K}^{+} pump moves [1]a2 \text{Na}^{+} out and 3 \text{K}^{+} inb3 \text{K}^{+} out and 2 \text{Na}^{+} inc3 \text{Na}^{+} out and 2 \text{K}^{+} indequal numbers of each
  4. Vitamin \text{B}_{12} contains [1]aironbzincccobaltdnickel
  5. Minamata disease is caused by poisoning with [1]aleadbmercuryccadmiumdarsenic
  6. The enzyme carbonic anhydrase contains [1]azincbironccopperdmanganese
Answers — 5.11

1. (b) — \text{Mg}^{2+} sits in the porphyrin ring (iron is in haem).

2. (a) — \text{Fe}^{2+} binds \text{O}_2.

3. (c) — three sodium out, two potassium in, per ATP.

4. (c) — cobalamin.

5. (b) — methylmercury in fish.

6. (a) — \text{Zn}^{2+} in the active site.

5.12 Basic Concept of Organic Chemistry

High-yield fact Value / form
Tetracovalency carbon forms four covalent bonds (sp^{3}, sp^{2}, sp)

Chapter summary

  • Group A is eleven one-mark MCQs drawn from all seventeen units; no unit is safe to skip, and the question types are: a name or definition, a formula or reagent, a one-step calculation, or a misconception.
  • Stoichiometry: N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}; molar volume 22.4\ \text{L} at STP; \text{V.D.} = M/2; percentage yield = actual/theoretical \times100.
  • Atomic structure: 2n^{2} electrons per shell; 2l+1 orbitals per subshell; Cr and Cu are the 3d exceptions; Hund, Pauli and Aufbau.
  • Periodic trends: radius falls and IE and EN rise across a period; the reverse down a group; F is the most electronegative, Cl has the highest electron affinity.
  • Shapes: linear sp, planar sp^{2}, tetrahedral sp^{3}, pyramidal and bent (lone pairs), sp^{3}d and sp^{3}d^{2} for \text{PCl}_5 and \text{SF}_6.
  • Redox: oxidation is loss of electrons; \text{Cr} = +6 in dichromate, \text{Mn} = +7 in permanganate; 1\ \text{F} = 96\,500\ \text{C}.
  • Gases: P_1V_1 = P_2V_2, PV = nRT, r_1/r_2 = \sqrt{M_2/M_1}; K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}.
  • Inorganic: ring test, Kipp's apparatus, Down's process, plaster of Paris \text{CaSO}_4\cdot\tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_2\text{O}; Haber (Fe), Ostwald (Pt–Rh), contact (\text{V}_2\text{O}_5), Solvay.
  • Organic: Markovnikov and the peroxide effect (HBr only); Wurtz and Kolbe give alkanes; Baeyer and bromine water test unsaturation; Hückel (4n+2); -\text{NO}_2 directs meta.

Group B — Short answer (5 marks each)

  1. Calculate the mass of \text{CaO} obtained by heating 50\ \text{g} of \text{CaCO}_3. [5]
  2. State Le Chatelier's principle and apply it to the Haber process for pressure and temperature. [5]
  3. Write the Lewis structure idea and shape of \text{H}_2\text{O} and explain why its bond angle is below 109.5^{\circ}. [5]
  4. Distinguish between ethane, ethene and ethyne by two chemical tests. [5]
Answers to Group B

1. \text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2; 50\ \text{g} = 0.5 mol; one mole of CaCO₃ gives one mole of CaO; mass of CaO = 0.5\times56 = 28\ \text{g}.

2. If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to oppose the disturbance. \text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3 (\Delta H < 0, fewer moles on the right): high pressure favours ammonia; low temperature favours ammonia but slows the rate, so about 450^{\circ}\text{C} with an Fe catalyst is the compromise.

3. Oxygen has six valence electrons, two used in bonds, so there are two bond pairs and two lone pairs (sp^{3}). Lone pair–lone pair and lone pair–bond pair repulsion exceeds bond pair–bond pair repulsion, squeezing the angle to 104.5^{\circ}; the shape is bent.

4. Bromine water: ethene and ethyne decolourise it, ethane does not. Ammoniacal \text{AgNO}_3: only ethyne gives a white precipitate. Baeyer's reagent is decolourised by ethene and ethyne but not ethane.

Group C — Long answer (8 marks each)

  1. Describe the manufacture of sulphuric acid by the contact process with the reactions, conditions and a flow sheet. [8]
  2. Describe the Solvay process for sodium carbonate, giving the reactions and the role of ammonia recovery. [8]
Answers to Group C

1. Steps: (i) Sulphur dioxide: \text{S} + \text{O}_2 \to \text{SO}_2 (or roasting pyrites, 4\text{FeS}_2 + 11\text{O}_2 \to 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 8\text{SO}_2); the gas is purified and dried. (ii) Oxidation: 2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3, \Delta H = -197\ \text{kJ}, over \text{V}_2\text{O}_5 at 400–450^{\circ}\text{C} and 1–2 atm; excess oxygen and removal of heat favour the yield. (iii) Absorption: \text{SO}_3 is dissolved in conc. \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 to give oleum: \text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \to \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7. (iv) Dilution: \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4. Water is not used for direct absorption because it forms a mist. Flow sheet: burner \to purifier \to dryer \to converter (\text{V}_2\text{O}_5) \to absorption tower \to oleum tank \to dilution.

2. Brine is saturated with \text{NH}_3 in an ammonia tower. In the carbonating (Solvay) tower \text{CO}_2 is passed in: \text{NaCl} + \text{NH}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to \text{NaHCO}_3 + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}; sparingly soluble \text{NaHCO}_3 separates and is filtered. Heating gives soda ash: 2\text{NaHCO}_3 \to \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} (the \text{CO}_2 is recycled). \text{CO}_2 comes from heating limestone, \text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2, and the lime slakes to \text{Ca(OH)}_2. Ammonia is recovered: 2\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{Ca(OH)}_2 \to 2\text{NH}_3 + \text{CaCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}. Overall: 2\text{NaCl} + \text{CaCO}_3 \to \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{CaCl}_2; ammonia is recycled, so only \text{CaCl}_2 is lost.
